name: Ahijah
overview: Ahijah is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Jerahmeel. His mention is brief and focused on his genealogical placement within the tribe, without additional narrative or descriptive notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahijah means '[my] brother is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the LORD. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:25, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to divine fellowship.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ahijah as the son of Jerahmeel, situating him within a known family line in Judah. Beyond this paternal relationship, no further family connections are documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Ahijah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role as a descendant of Judah through Jerahmeel, contributing to the biblical record of Israel's tribal lineage. Although no direct narrative actions or spiritual roles are attributed to him, his mention preserves the continuity of God's covenant people as recorded in the Old Testament genealogies.
